# GlobalCounters -- `class GlobalCounters`, helpers.py:302
#
# SIX ClassVars (helpers.py:303-308) and one `@staticmethod reset` (:309-310). The
# class has no methods beyond `reset` and no instances anywhere: every write is
# `GlobalCounters.<name> = ...` or `GlobalCounters.<name> += ...` on the CLASS.
#
# THE MUTABLE-STATE ANSWER, since it is the question this block exists to settle.
# Upstream's state lives in the class object and every reader sees the last write.
# Bend has no mutable globals, no `Ref`, no store and no closures, so the state is a
# `Data` VALUE that is threaded: `Counters` in, `Counters` out, and each `bump_*` is
# the one-line rebuild that upstream's `+=` is. That is not a weaker counter, it is
# the same counter:
#   - it COUNTS. `bump_ops` adds `d` to the value that came IN, so a sequence of five
#     bumps accumulates, and the gate runs exactly that sequence and prints the total
#     after each step (`gc_init_ops`, `gc_bumped_ops`) against live CPython.
#   - it CANNOT GO STALE, which is the property a mutable global does not have. There
#     is no second copy to read, so a reader that forgets to thread the newest record
#     gets the OLD value -- a wrong answer the gate can see, not a silently shared
#     cell that is right until someone forgets to update it.
# What threading costs is the caller: `GlobalCounters.reset()` upstream is a statement
# and `GlobalCounters.reset(GlobalCounters.reset())` here is a value the caller must
# use. That is the whole price and it is paid at the one place that owns the record.
#
# `mem_used` and `mem_used_per_device` are the interesting half and `reset` is why:
# the tuple at :310 names FOUR fields, and the source says on :324-325 that the other
# two are "NOT reset". A `reset` that zeroed all six would be a plausible-looking bug
# that no test of the four would catch, so the gate reads `mem_used` and the per-device
# counts AFTER a reset (`gc_after_used`, `gc_after_dev0`, `gc_after_dev3`).
#
# `time_sum_s` is a CPython `float`, i.e. an F64, and it is the one field that cannot
# be incremented here: `base.bend` has no F32 addition. `F32.add` is a `law`
# (base.bend:1556) -- an axiom with no body -- and live code may not call a law, so a
# float accumulator has no expression. The field is carried, typed `F32`, and is
# never written here; `.agents/slop/helpers-oracle.py` measures what CPython does with
# it and prints those rows to STDERR so they are recorded without being diffed.
# TODO(p4) helpers.py:305  `time_sum_s` needs the engine's clock, which is a C effect.
subject: GlobalCounters

#      folds. So `full(shape, 42)` is 9 nodes and `full(shape, 42, dtype=half)` is 10,
#      and the ONLY difference is one CAST -- same root op, same nsrc, same srcs.
#      `weak.bend`'s `wk_const_at` (weak.bend:401) spells the CAST UNCONDITIONALLY and
#      is the wrong shape here, and `wk_ccast` is the other wrong shape: it rebuilds
#      the CONST and loses the CAST entirely. `cr_cast` is `DTypeMixin.cast`
#      (dtype.py:36) with the fold, which is the only one of the three that is right.
#   3. `full(shape, 0.0, dtype=int32)` CONSTS AN INT, NOT A FLOAT. `DType.const`
#      (dtype.py:79-84) truncates, `int(truncate[int32](0.0))` is `0`, an `int`, and
#      `from_py` reads the VALUE -- so `zeros(2,3,dtype=int32)` has an INT CONST cast
#      to int32 (10 nodes) where `zeros(2,3)` has a FLOAT CONST (9). The truncation
#      is P3 (dtype.py:84, and ops.bend's own `UOp.const` TODO), so `cr_full`'s
#      `fill_value` is the ALREADY-TRUNCATED `O.Const` and `cr_zeros_i` passes

#      row and not a restatement.
#      TODO(p3) dtype.py:84  `DType.const`'s `truncate`.

#      test is `ret.shape == self.shape` (movement.py:187) and an ALLOC's shape is

#      `row_empty4_g` is ONE node and `row_empty23_g` is five. After the reshape
#      `u.shape` IS `new_shape`, `shrink_to` builds `_mop(SHRINK, ((0,n0),(0,n1)))`

#      nothing and is not a workaround.

# elementwise.bend -- tinygrad/mixin/elementwise.py. `ElementwiseMixin`: the
# promotion, the binop dispatch, and the method surface that makes
# `Tensor(...)+Tensor(...)` CONCRETE.
#
# WHAT IS IN HERE, and it is the whole of the part of Python that is a GRAPH
# FACT. `_broadcasted`'s promotion (elementwise.py:24-34), `_binop` (:36), `remint`
# (:12), `ufix` (:21), and the sixty methods whose body is an `alu` over a promoted
# operand. Those are the twelve ops tensor.bend's dunder table names, the three
# comparison binops plus their three negations, the unary alu family, and the
# composed ones (`neg`, `sub`, `logical_not`, `where`, `mod`, `fmod`, `div`,
# `square`, `minimum`, `bitwise_not`, the shifts and `pow`).
#
# FOUR WALLS, and each is a NAMED TOLERANCE rather than a hole.
#
#   1. `x: Self | ConstType` IS A `Data` UNION (`Ew` below), because Python's
#      `isinstance(x, type(self))` is a membership test over two types and a `Data`
#      union is a set of tags. `ufix` is then `ECon` -> a CONST node and `ETen` ->
#      the tensor, which is Python's `x if isinstance(x, Self) else wrap(ufix(x))`.
#   2. `_broadcasted` answers a PAIR, and a pair is a `Type` in Bend, so it is
#      `Br{l, r}`, a two-field `Data` record -- `mixin/dtype.bend`'s `Dts` and
#      `uop/weak.bend`'s `ODt` are the same shape for the same reason.
#   3. `promote` BUILDS, so the arena grows under it and `self._uop.dtype` is stale
#      the moment it fires. Python re-reads `.dtype` lazily, from one global ucache;
#      here it is one store per METHOD, and the whole file is written to keep it that
#      way. `Tensor.ar(t)` is only the right store while nothing has been minted
#      since `t` was made, which is exactly the condition that stops holding at the
#      second operand -- so `+ar` is threaded (`ew_promote`, `ew_cast.at`) and never
#      read off a tensor, and the two arms that mint nothing STILL rebase. See
#      `ew_promote` and `ew_alu2`; the measured failure is in
#      bend2-constraints.md, "rule 6 has a SECOND HALF".
#   4. `remint` is a RECURSION (`u.src[0]`) that GROWS the arena, so it is
#      self-recursive with the FUEL FIRST and it threads `+O.Arena` rather than a
#      fold: every read it makes (`op`, `arg`, `src0`) is a raw arena read of a node
#      that existed BEFORE the walk, and an append-only store does not renumber
#      what it already holds. That is why `ew_ccast_at` builds with the threaded
#      arena and does NOT call `uop/weak.bend`'s `wk_const_at`, which builds in
#      `F.Folded.ar(fx)` -- the arena rule, and the one `tensor.bend` records as its
#      second Bend rule. `ew_remint.put` then has to build in the arena its OWN
#      recursion grew, which is the same rule one level down.
#
# THE FLOAT-CONST FAMILY IS A THIRD WALL AND IT IS BIG. Every method whose Python
# body names a float LITERAL -- `cos` (math.pi/2), `exp` and `sigmoid` and

# wall for its own CONST fixtures ("every CONST fixture here is an INT or a BOOL,
# and `Tensor(1.0)` is a `TODO(p3)`"), and it is the same wall rather than a second

#    read twice is a `+` parameter; a value bound to a `let` and read twice is
#    RECOMPUTED, not bound. `+` cannot be spelled on a closure type or a `Maybe`
#    parameter, so the two-`Maybe` readers pass the `Maybe` to a separate `.of`.

#    no projection syntax in Bend 2.0.34 (`pa.slot` is "expected : a defined
#    name"), so a `ParamArg` with one field changed is thirteen
#    `O.ParamArg.*(pa)` calls. AND THE FIELD ORDER IS ops.bend's DECLARATION
#    order, not the header's prose order: `volatile, image, buffer,
#    bind_on_realize, val`. Read the declaration.
#

#    binding, and a def whose body is a `do` block must be the LAST def in the

#    errors with unhelpful locations. `main` is therefore last.

#    `O.Found.ar(inner)`, never the arena handed in. An arena only GROWS, so the
#    passed arena is a PREFIX and the inner node's index is not in it; the outer
#    node's src0 then points past the end and `Arena.arg` answers the bottom's

# wrong instruction. So this file ports the ALGEBRA and names the FFI.

# `mesa.glsl_type_builtin_*` is NOT REACHABLE ON THIS TREE. It is bound inside a

#       glsl_type_builtin*: 0        # of 9,974 module attributes
#
# So `nir.glsl_type` (:14-16) is not missing a constant, it is UNUSABLE: its dict
# comprehension is EAGER, so it evaluates `g("glsl_type_builtin_double")` before

run:
# THE SHAPE OF THE MACHINE, and the two parts that were not obvious.
#
# `run` carries the mutable state ops_python.py:52-157 keeps in four locals: the
# `values` dict, the buffer bytearrays, `exec_masks`, and `pbufs`/`pvals`. Under
# the rules above that is one `Prog` record threaded through a fuel recursion.
#
#   * THE PC IS A LOOP, NOT A RECURSION. Python is `while i < len(self.uops)`
#     with `BACKEDGE`/`END`/`RANGE` writing `i`. Bend has no loop and no
#     `continue`, so `run` is `run(fuel, pr)` with the PC threaded and a DIE on
#     fuel exhaustion -- which is also the "stay turing-incomplete" answer, since
#     a RANGE-driven kernel has no static step bound.
#   * THE ARENA IS STRIDED, NOT BUMP-ALLOCATED. Python's `values` is keyed by
#     UOp, so a RANGE body overwrites exactly the entries the first pass wrote
#     (ops_python.py:125-127 increments `values[u]` in place, and :129 `del`s
#     it). A bump allocator would append afresh on the second pass and the loop
#     would read its own history, so uop `i` owns a FIXED slot run -- see
#     `Uop.run_of.op` -- and a re-executed uop lands back on it.
#
# ONE KNOWN WRONG ANSWER, and it is measured rather than argued. `alu1(SQRT, ...)`
# over an ELEMENT whose dtype is int32 answers 456459507 where Python's
# `python_alu[Ops.SQRT](16)` is `math.sqrt(16)` = 4.0 (1082130432). The row is
# in .agents/slop/exec_gate.bend, printed as KNOWN-FAIL so it cannot be mistaken
# for a pass. `op_is_mathy` sends SQRT to the float lane and `f_of` reads the
# 16 as 16.0, so the fault is inside the lane input, not the lane choice.
# TODO(p3) runtime/ops_python.py:138 -- the float lane's input for an int dtype.
subject: __call__

marker_text: # TODO(p3) runtime/ops_python.py:160 -- the base64 quartet fold.
own: # TODO(p3) runtime/ops_python.py:160 -- the base64 quartet fold.
run:
#
# WALL 5, AND IT IS A REAL ONE. `base64.b64decode` is a character-level transform
# with nothing dynamic in it, so it LOOKS like the most portable def in this file
# and it is the only one here that is left unported. The reason is measured, not
# guessed, and it is worth writing down because the first draft compiled, ran and
# produced plausible-looking hex:
#
#   * `Bool.pick` EVALUATES BOTH ARMS. A losing arm that computes
#     `Char.from_u32(U32.sub(v, 10))` for `v < 10` is `Char.from_u32(2**32 - 6)`,
#     which is not a scalar value, and the run dies with
#       bend: 4294967291 is not a Unicode scalar value
#     EVEN THOUGH the chosen arm was fine. (A `U32` in the losing arm is
#     harmless: it underflows to a valid `U32` and is discarded. The trap is
#     specific to a CHECKED type.) The nibble/byte printers below dodge it.
#   * With that fixed, the decoder ran, and its OUTPUT WAS WRONG against
#     CPython for every non-trivial input. Port vs CPython, measured:
#         "AA=="      port 04          CPython 00
#         "AP8="      port 04          CPython 00ff
#         "AP9/"      port 00          CPython 00ff7f
#         "AP9/AQ=="  port fc0404      CPython 00ff7f01
#         "dGhlIHF1..." port 9481c5ac... CPython 7468652071...
#     The byte COUNTS were wrong too (3 where CPython says 4 on the last one).
# `U32.shrn` is NOT the culprit -- measured `U32.shrn(4160, 16n) = 0` and
# `U32.shrn(16711680, 16n) = 255`, both correct -- so the defect is in how this
# fold threads its quartet index through the `Bool.pick` selects, and it was NOT
# found inside the time this unit had.
#
# A row that disagrees with CPython is a row that encodes a bug, so there are NO
# `pyc_*` rows here at all. What IS kept is the fact that is decidable without
# running the transform: `compile` IS `base64.b64decode` -- measured
# `PythonCompiler.compile.__func__ is base64.b64decode` is False, but
# `compile(src) == base64.b64decode(src)` on every fixture, i.e. it IS the
# function under another name.
# TODO(p3) runtime/ops_python.py:160 -- the base64 quartet fold.
subject: compile

# THE WALLS. Three, and each is named with the line that owns it.
#
# 1. THE 64-BIT WALL, in three separate places, and they are not the same place.
#    `base.bend` exports no 64-bit integer, so:
#      - `GSP_FW_WPR_META_MAGIC` = 15869187694674993331 (:442). ONE of the 65
#        integer constants ip.py names does not fit a U32. `ip_c_over64` names
#        it; it is not ported, and the WPR meta builder records the field as the
#        seam's.
#      - `maxUserVa=0x7ffffffff000` (:608) and the four `gpuPhys*Addr` fields of
#        `GspSystemInfo` (:605). Their OFFSETS and WIDTHS are in the layout table
#        -- 8-byte fields at their byte offsets -- and their VALUES are the
#        seam's. `GspSystemInfo` is 48 fields and 928 bytes and the port knows
#        all of that.
#      - `_checksum` (:32-36) sums u64 words. This one is NOT a wall and the
#        reason is the whole reason the checksum gate is worth having: the
#        accumulator is a XOR and `hi32(x) ^ lo32(x)` COMMUTES with XOR over the
#        words, so the whole checksum collapses to two U32 folds over the
#        TWENTY U32 words of `GSP_MSG_QUEUE_ELEMENT ++ rpc_message_header_v`.
#        `rp.cksum.xor` does that, and it needs the byte OFFSETS -- so it fails
#        on a wrong field order and a wrong offset, which a count gate would not.
#        It does NOT fail on a wrong endianness, because XOR is commutative: the
#        mutation table records the exchange of `rp.pickw`'s arms as an equivalent
#        mutant, and the comment above `rp.pickw` says so where a reader needs it.
#
#    Two more 64-bit facts live where they bite rather than here, because each is
#    one arithmetic chain and not a type boundary:
#      - `init_wpr_meta` (:434-455) SUBTRACTS from `vram_size`, so every offset it
#        computes exceeds 2**32 for any real card. See THE FIXTURES beside
#        `wpr.leg4` and `ip_wpr_vram_max`.
#      - `id8=int.from_bytes(bytes(f"LOG{name}", 'utf-8'), 'big')` (:395) is an
#        EIGHT-BYTE name read big-endian. See the note beside `libos` and
#        `ip_libos_id8_bytes`.
#      # TODO(p3) support/nv/ip.py:442  GSP_FW_WPR_META_MAGIC
subject: init_wpr_meta
